newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: INTERVIEW-GECAMINES SEES LOWER METALS OUTPUT IN 97.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-GECAMINES SEES LOWER METALS OUTPUT IN 97.

text.p: The new Congo's state mining company Gecamines said on Wednesday it expected copper and cobalt output to drop in 1997 from last year's production levels.
But Gecamines chairman Mbaka Kawaya told Reuters he expected output to increase next year.

"We will not realise this year the same production as last year but we will increase production (next year). The increase in production will probably start the second half of the year," Kawaya said in an interview.
He said the company had stockpiles of around 10,000 tonnes of copper and two months' worth of cobalt production which it was trying to sell.
Gecamines produced around 4,000 tonnes of copper and two months' cobalt production would be around 670 tonnes.
Kawaya said Gecamines would air freight cobalt which had already been sold.

He said the company hoped to increase production by forming joint ventures with foreign companies and raise funds to develop the copper and cobalt industry which fell into neglect under the rule of former president Mobutu Sese Seko.
Gecamines planned about 20 joint ventures -- of which some had already been awarded to America Mineral Fields and Tenke Mining Co .
"We had big stocks of copper -- around 10,000 tonnes -- which is lying in our plants, and cobalt as well.
"What are we going to try and do now is to try and sell all (that) cobalt. We are exporting cobalt by plane to get the money," he said.
Kawaya said Gecamines had been trying for the past month and a half, since the old management was axed, to pay salaries.
"What we have done during the month and half was to try and pay salaries and some ancient debts," he added.
He said Gecamines wanted to explore parts of Katanga province (formerly Shaba) to increase the former Zaire's ore reserves.
"We want to explore and use new methods like satellite imagery," Kawaya said, adding that any new finds would be shared with Gecamines.
Among the companies that have signed exploration agreements were JCI Ltd , Trillion Resources Corp, America Mineral Fields, Tenke Mining Co and Poland's largest copper producer KGHM Polska Miedz SA.
He said the copper concession was about 20,000 square km while Gecamines's zinc exploration area was in the region of 12,000 square km.
"The strategy of the future is to conclude partnerships. We have concluded partnerships with foreign companies to form joint ventures like Tenke Fungurume and Ruashi-Etoile.
"We are trying to get financing from outside companies and many companies are interested," Kawaya said.
